item.title: [Java Deserialization] CommonsBeanutils1 exploit chain analysis
item.author: quactv
item.description: Vulnerabilities related to deserialization in Java have become a hot security topic in recent years. An unsafe deserialization process can lead to serious vulnerabilities such as remote code execution. Ysoserial is a project created by frohoff, one of the people who discovered deserialization vulnerabilities in Java. This post will analyze the CommonsBeanutils1 chain Apache Commons Beanutils is another project in the Apache Commons toolkit that provides some methods for manipulating ordinary Java class objects (also known as JavaBeans).

item.title: Tunneling, Pivoting to Attack Internal Network
item.author: quactv
item.description: Intro There are plenty of articles and blogs on the Internet talking about attacking and penetrating internal networks, but most of them focus on using the tools, while the principles and scenarios are rarely mentioned or explained much. In this post I’ll discuss the principles of attacking internal networks in various ways, flexibly designing an internal-network attack diagram to match the different internal-network scenarios. This is also one of my favorite topics in cybersecurity and red team operations in general.

item.title: JWT Attack
item.author: quactv
item.description: What is JWT The full name of JWT is Json Web Token. It follows the JSON format and encodes user information into the token. The server doesn’t store any user information, only the key information, and it verifies the token using a specific encryption algorithm and verifies the user’s identity through the token. Token-based authentication can replace the traditional cookie + session authentication method. JWT consists of three parts: header.

item.title: Android Pentest Note
item.author: quactv
item.description: Concept Structure AndroidManifest file contains the application’s structure Res folder contains all the resources that the application needs to run , including user interface layout, icons, audio, etc. The most interesting files for us are the classes.dex files because they are the compiled java files. The .dex extension stands for Dalvik EXecutable. So we need to decompile these dex files to get the java classes. Tools Apktool : tool for reverse engineering Android apk files.

item.title: Linux Backdoors
item.author: quactv
item.description: In practice, once you have access to a target (SSH, VNC, interactive shell …), leaving a backdoor is an important part of maintaining access to the target system. Therefore, learning some backdoor techniques is essential, not only for attackers but also for defenders. In what follows we’ll look at some common backdoor techniques. Here we only discuss within the Linux world! What is a backdoor? A backdoor is a piece of hidden code, a script or a program placed on the target machine serving the attacker’s purpose of long-term access to the target, with which you don’t have to exploit the same system twice.
